headline: LinkedIn is the one clear underperformer (ROAS 0.87, CPA $267), so I cut its budget 25%. Google Search's true value is unsettled, so I'm recommending a holdout test instead of moving its budget.

moves.reason: Last-click ROAS 0.87 last 7d (CPA $267) vs 1.03 prior 4wk avg (CPA $186); 13-week ROAS has been ~1.1 with CPA $105-265. Even the most favorable model (Markov/first-touch) implies CPA ~$88, vs $36-50 for Google/Meta. Self-reported LinkedIn ~5%, in line with 4.5% last-touch credit, so no hidden value. Moderate 25% cut, easy to reverse. Weekly counts are only 7-20 conversions, so a deep cut is not warranted.

tests.hypothesis: Google Search's true incremental share is closer to first-touch (29%) than last-touch (55%) because much of its last-click credit is brand/navigational capture of buyers persuaded elsewhere (self-reported 'Google' is 43%).
tests.design: Geo holdout: pause brand-keyword campaigns in ~20% of matched regions for 3-4 weeks while keeping them live elsewhere. Measure total conversions and revenue (all channels incl. direct) in held-out vs control regions, plus non-brand conversions. Compare lift to Google's reported conversions (~168/wk) to get incremental CPA. Pre-register a minimum detectable effect of ~10%.

flag_verdicts.reason: The CPA rise from $156 to $238 is noisy, with only 7-20 conversions a week. But LinkedIn's 13-week ROAS has stayed around 1.1 (0.87 last 7d), and its CPA is the worst under every attribution model ($88-165 vs $4-50 elsewhere). A modest cut is justified.

flags.message: linkedin CPA rose 1.5x, from $156 to $238, starting 2026-10-18.
